claims.text: The alloy initially has a single-phase solid-solution microstructure.
Mechanical loading causes nanoscale precipitates to form in the alloy.
Mechanical loading causes dislocation pile-ups in the alloy.
Nanoscale precipitates act as stress concentrators and crack-nucleation sites.
Dislocation pile-ups act as stress concentrators and crack-nucleation sites.
Stress concentration and crack nucleation cause loss of toughness or brittle fracture.
At room temperature and atmospheric pressure, loading at a stress amplitude of 500 MPa and a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1 will produce a 20% reduction in toughness relative to the initial baseline.

At room temperature and atmospheric pressure, loading at a stress amplitude of 500 MPa and a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1 will produce a 30% increase in brittle-fracture probability relative to the initial baseline.
The applicable service or loading boundary is a stress amplitude above 700 MPa.
The applicable service or loading boundary is a strain rate above 10^-2 s^-1.
Alloy composition can influence the formation of nanoscale precipitates and dislocation pile-ups and therefore affect toughness loss or brittle-fracture onset.
Processing history can influence the formation of nanoscale precipitates and dislocation pile-ups and therefore affect toughness loss or brittle-fracture onset.
In situ TEM or SEM under mechanical loading can be used to examine microstructural evolution and fracture behavior.
The hypothesis is falsified if loading at 500 MPa and 10^-3 s^-1 causes less than a 10% toughness reduction and less than a 10% increase in brittle-fracture probability.

contradictions.description: The proposed test uses 500 MPa and 10^-3 s^-1, whereas the stated applicability boundary requires stress amplitude above 700 MPa and strain rate above 10^-2 s^-1. The prediction and falsification test therefore lie outside the hypothesis's own stated loading boundary.

The baseline is defined as having no mechanical loading, but toughness and fracture probability require a loading or fracture test to be measured. Thus the stated unloaded baseline cannot directly provide the comparison quantities without an additional baseline specimen tested under defined conditions.
